question: Does grouping heterogeneous peers by visit-context similarity and training one model per group beat a single shared model on every peer's held-out data, without leaving low-data peers worse off?
method: Covertype subsample; peers = dominant wilderness area; per-peer stratified 25% test split; k-means on per-peer context summaries; cluster MLPs blended per peer with local MLPs; seeds 42-44.
baseline: One shared MLPClassifier (64 hidden units) trained on pooled peer training data (FedAvg-style stand-in).
improved: One MLP per k-means cluster of peer context summaries (k chosen by silhouette), each peer's prediction = local MLP blended with its cluster MLP, local weight n_p/(n_p+1000).
notes: Only 4 peers (wilderness areas), so clustering and silhouette selection are very coarse. The MLP is a stand-in for FedAvg, not the paper's algorithm. The shrinkage prior (1000) was fixed a priori and not tuned; no hyperparameter was tuned on the test set. Shrinkage direction: small peers lean on the cluster model, large peers on their local model. The improved model fits more models (cluster + local), so it uses more compute. Single data split; results are from one subsample.
